trajectory_summary: The call is stagnant-to-mixed: Barbara stays cooperative throughout and the rep completes the mechanical verify and bill-capture steps, but the rep never builds any emotional traction — no interest question, no bill flip, no curiosity creation. The appointment gets set almost by default, with Barbara doing more work (finding the bill, sending the photo) than the rep does in creating a reason to show up.

observed_outcome.reasoning: Barbara agrees to a specific day (Tuesday) and time (10AM) for the appointment; no co-owner was identified since she confirmed no one else is on the title.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I my I just got my bill yesterday. It's a $137.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Rep captured the $137 bill amount at 01:10 but immediately pivoted to explaining data needs rather than using the number to build urgency; the flip should have landed right after Barbara volunteered the figure, e.g. acknowledging the pain before moving to the kWh ask.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: If I text you, can you just take a picture of that graph?
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep asked the customer to send a picture of the usage graph and the customer confirmed at 03:16 that they had sent it during the call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep did not ask why the customer was interested in solar, and no interest reason was provided.

primary_coaching_focus.why: Without ever asking why Barbara wants solar, the rep has no emotional anchor to flip the bill against or personalize the text follow-up — this is the root cause of the call's flat, transactional feel.

key_moments.quote: How are you doing? Oh, okay. I'm fine.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep answers his own rapport question, a diarization/attention artifact suggesting he steamrolled past the pause meant to let Barbara respond naturally.

key_moments.quote: I'm reaching out about the solar form you filled out online.
key_moments.stewart_read: Legitimacy is established minimally via the form reference, which is adequate per script, but there's no state mention or further credibility anchor before diving into qualifying questions.

key_moments.quote: You able to access a power bill real quick?
key_moments.stewart_read: When Barbara immediately volunteers her bill amount, the rep pivots straight to explaining why he doesn't need the price — filing the number instead of reflecting it back as pain or leverage.

key_moments.quote: So it's a graph on your power bill. It should just be on the front or back page.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep's first instruction is vague enough that Barbara has to ask again a minute later, burning call time on a low-value navigation task.
